meta.title: CarPal admin console (WP15 UI, WP20 admin part; frontend/admin-console/) — build plan and stage log
meta.purpose: Build the internal staff console that operates the platform: Path 2 review approvals, moderation, disputes, verification, privacy requests, plans, flags and the AI kill switch, the USD exchange rate, taxonomy, audit, AI/MCP oversight and analytics. Without it the pilot cannot run without direct API or database work (backend S11 open_after_stage, NI-08).
sources_of_truth: Docs/40.API contract.md (contract 1.2.0) wins for operations, fields, roles and security rules. §23 is the admin plane (62 operations on host admin-api), §2.14 SEC-ADM-1..7.

Docs/23.Admin_WebUI_screens.md wins for screens, layout and UX rules where the contract allows them. Where it asks for data or actions the contract lacks, the gap is recorded in backend_requests (GD-08).
Docs/02.Detailed project plan.md (WP15, WP17, WP20, §1.4, §15) and Docs/90 §9 for scope and hosts.

Cross-plan rule (memory, 2026-11-04): the newer frontend plan wins over backend/dev_plan.json when they disagree; the backend follows. Write ids from other plans with a prefix: 'backend NI-04', 'PWA GD-03'. This plan's ids use the prefix 'ADM' when quoted elsewhere (e.g. 'ADM DI-02').
how_to_use: One stage per working session. Each stage is sized to fit one session (about a 5-hour token budget). If a stage runs long, stop at a task boundary, mark it 'partial' with partial_reason, and continue it as ACn-b next session (as backend S9a/b/c did).
At the start of a stage: read only its context_to_read, then the report of the previous stage (notes_for_next, open_after_stage).

At the end of a stage: set task statuses, fill report (template in conventions.report_template), add new DI/OQ/BR entries, update meta.progress, and run the stage's acceptance commands. Commit only when the user asks.
Backend work that a stage needs (backend_requests with stage 'AC2' or other) is done in backend/ and also logged as a backend stage (S12, S13) in backend/dev_plan.json.

global_decisions.decision: The console is its own Next.js app in frontend/admin-console/ (App Router, TypeScript strict, ESM, Tailwind CSS v4), its own pnpm package (@carpal/admin-console) with its own lockfile, no root workspace. Versions match the PWA so code and fixes move between them: next 16.4.3, react/react-dom 19.3.1, tailwindcss 4.3.3, @tanstack/react-query 5.104.5, zod 4.6.7, i18next 26.4.3, react-i18next 17.0.16, jose 6.2.12, @simplewebauthn/browser 14.0.0, maplibre-gl 6.14.0 (AC9 only), @playwright/test 1.64.1, @axe-core/playwright 4.14.0. Later minor updates are recorded in the stage report.
global_decisions.reason: The admin plane has its own OAuth client (cp-web-admin, aal3, audience admin-api) and must stay reachable only through a gate (SEC-ADM-1; the gate itself is still open, Docs/02 §15). A separate deployable keeps every gate option possible and never ships admin code or routes from the public web.<DOMAIN> origin. Docs/02 §1.4 says admin pages are part of the web app: see DI-01.

global_decisions.decision: Node: run on backend/.tools/node (24.21.0) through tools/use-local-node.sh and .ps1 copied from pwa/tools. .node-version = 24.21.0.

Admin BFF = a copy, with provenance comments, of the framework-free PWA BFF (pwa/src/server/bff: session store port, OAuth client, DPoP, private_key_jwt signer, 1:1 forwarder with registry allowlist, CSRF, header hygiene) under frontend/admin-console/src/server/bff/, adapted for cp-web-admin: acr_values=aal3, audience admin-api, access 5 min, refresh 30 min idle, 8 h absolute, allowlist = admin-api routes + the api-host reads in GD-07. No guest/anonymous tokens and no cp-ssr. When the business web app (cp-web-portal) starts, the three copies are extracted to one shared package (recommendation R-01).
global_decisions.reason: Reuse what already passed the strict-mode checks in PWA P15 without touching the live PWA now; extract once there are three users (rule of three).

global_decisions.decision: Staff sign-in (A-AUTH-01) is hosted by the console itself at /id/* on the admin host, not by the PWA. Only what staff need: email + password, then a passkey (WebAuthn) for aal3; no sign-up, no SMS code, no social sign-in. A staff account without a passkey is taken through a forced passkey enrolment after password + email code, then signs in again at aal3. Needs the backend to choose the sign-in URL per client (BR-02) and to finish staff WebAuthn end to end (BR-03).
global_decisions.reason: Keeps staff credentials and the staff flow off the public consumer app and behind the same gate as the console; A-AUTH-01 differs from the consumer sign-in in almost every rule. Override with OQ-01.

global_decisions.decision: EN and FA with full RTL. The locale comes from the staff member's me.locale (switchable in the avatar menu, kept in a cookie); no locale segment in URLs (internal app, no SEO). Common keys come from shared/i18n/locales; console strings go in an 'admin' namespace following the PWA layout (pwa/src/lib/i18n), and the key-parity check covers it. Dates: Jalali in FA and Gregorian in EN, stored and sent in UTC; digits localised for display only; IDs, codes and timestamps in tables can switch to Latin digits.

Design: shared/design-system/web tokens, fonts and components, synced with a copy of pwa/tools/sync-design-system.mjs; the PWA's ported components (pwa/src/components/ds) are copied as the starting kit. The console adds a dense admin layer: data table, three-panel case layout, drawer, reason panel, masked field, four-eyes banner, entity chip, timeline. Logical CSS properties only (copy of pwa/tools/check-logical-css.mjs). Light and dark themes. An environment badge (DEV / STAGING / PROD in red) is always visible.

API scope: the console calls the 62 admin-api operations of contract 1.2.0 through its BFF. A short, explicit list of api-host reads may be forwarded as well if the cp-web-admin token is accepted there (checked in AC2): me.get (staff identity and roles), config.client, taxonomy reads for the tree. Anything else is reached by opening the public page (pwa.<DOMAIN>) in a new tab, never by widening the BFF.

The contract wins over Docs/23. A screen ships with what the contract provides; missing data or actions are recorded as backend_requests (BR-xx) and as doc issues, and are built in AC14 only if the user approves them (OQ-07). Buttons for actions that do not exist are not shown (no dead buttons).
global_decisions.reason: The backend is finished and swept; the console must not invent endpoints.

global_decisions.decision: Staff roles are the contract's four: ADM platform_admin, MOD platform_moderator, SUP platform_support, CRV platform_community_reviewer. Navigation and buttons are shown from the role sets in each operation's sec: line (generated into a role table at AC1). Docs/23's nine roles map as: Content moderator, Verification officer, Trust & Safety lead → MOD (lead powers that need ADM are shown only to ADM); Community reviewer → CRV; Privacy officer, AI governance, Commercial admin, Platform admin → ADM; Support agent → SUP. The server always decides; the UI only hides.

Purpose-bound reads (SEC-ADM-5): every PURP read is opened from a work item (case, dispute, DSR, verification, review approval). The purpose travels in the URL (?purpose=<kind>:<id>) and the BFF sends it as CarPal-Access-Purpose. Opening a person or organization without a work item asks the staff member to pick or open one. A-USR-01 is therefore an exact lookup (one identifier), not a browsable list (DI-03).

Every mutating action opens the reason panel (reason code + note; note required for removals, suspensions and rejections) and sends the reason as the contract asks (body 'reason', or the CarPal-Reason header on DELETE). A 202 PendingChange (4EYES) shows 'Waiting for a second staff member' with a link to Pending approvals; SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN is explained, not shown as an error. Operations tagged AAL3 or STEP_UP trigger a re-authentication with the passkey and replay the action.
global_decisions.reason: SEC-ADM-2, SEC-ADM-3, SEC-ADM-6; Docs/23 principles 1 and 7.

global_decisions.decision: No personal data is stored in the browser: TanStack Query cache in memory only, cleared on sign-out, idle timeout and staff switch; no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB for responses; Cache-Control: no-store on every page and BFF response; no service worker; no analytics or error-reporting SDK; console logs never print response bodies. Saved views and column choices (no data) may be kept in localStorage.
Ports: dev 3200, e2e 3300, both over https://localhost with the PWA's dev certificate approach. Backend lite: admin-api :8081, auth :8082.

Tests: Vitest unit and DOM projects; integration project against the live lite backend; Playwright E2E (Chromium) with a CDP virtual authenticator for passkeys; @axe-core/playwright for accessibility; RTL screenshots for key screens. `pnpm check` = lint + logical-css + typecheck + unit + contract:check + i18n:check + ds:check.
global_decisions.reason: Same quality bar as the PWA (P13).

global_decisions.decision: Deployment: frontend/admin-console/deploy/ (deploy.md, admin-setup.sh, admin-update.sh, lib.sh, templates/) following the WinSCP + staging-folder workflow and the shared /carpal/config/deploy.conf; ADMIN_HOST=admin.<DOMAIN> derived from DOMAIN; scripts LF-only. The access gate in front of the console is a setting (ADMIN_GATE=ip_allowlist | none), default ip_allowlist, because the final access strategy is still open (Docs/02 §15, OQ-02).
global_decisions.reason: Memory: deploy workflow and host naming; SEC-ADM-1.

code_rules: No widening: the BFF forwards only allowlisted operations 1:1 (SEC-WEB-1).
Every action button is gated by the generated role table and hidden when the caller lacks the role; server errors 403 still render the no-permission state.
Unknown enum values from the server render as 'Unknown (<value>)', never crash (PWA P13 rule).
Masked by default: phone, email, full name, VIN, plate, documents. Reveal = purpose-bound read, logged by the backend.
Removals and suspensions are never bulk (Docs/23 §3.3).

open_questions.question: Contract 1.2.0 lets only CRV (platform_community_reviewer) decide Path 2 review approvals (admin.review_approval_decide is STF(CRV); admin.review_approvals_queue and admin.review_approval_get are STF(CRV, MOD)). An ADM cannot even open the approval queue or the disputes (admin.disputes_queue and admin.dispute_resolve are STF(MOD, CRV)). Keep that, or widen the sets to ADM (a contract change, backend 1.2.1)? Related staffing fact from the generated table: every four-eyes change needs a second staff member who may decide it (admin.four_eyes_decide is STF(ADM, MOD: moderation changes only)), so ADM-only changes (kill switch off, a rate change over 20 %, plan and retention edits, staff role grants) need two ADM accounts, and moving a Path 1 review to Path 2 (STF(MOD) 4EYES) needs two MOD or a MOD and an ADM.
open_questions.default_if_unanswered: Keep the contract. For the pilot: at least two ADM accounts and at least one MOD and one CRV (a person may hold several roles; the console and server keep the 'different staff member' rule per action). Grant CRV as a second role to whoever reviews (role grants are four-eyes, AC10), and seed one user per role plus a second ADM in BR-05.

open_questions.question: Local development: GD-13 says https://localhost:3200, but the PWA runs over http://localhost and brings the OAuth code back through its /id proxy because the backend registers https redirect URIs only (PWA DI-24, OQ-10). open_questions.default_if_unanswered: Follow the PWA (http in dev and E2E). AC1 already runs this way; browsers treat localhost as a secure context, so __Host- Secure cookies still work in Chromium.

recommendations_for_next_stages.text: When the business web app (cp-web-portal) starts, extract the BFF core (session, oauth, dpop, private_key_jwt, forwarder, csrf), the typed client and the design-system kit from pwa/ and frontend/admin-console/ into shared packages instead of making a third copy.
Ask the WP0 owner to settle the staff permission matrix (DI-02) and the four-eyes list (OQ-04) before AC14, so the backend roles and the Docs/23 roles match.
Run backend NI-02 (purpose bound to the record, BR-09) before real staff use the console with real user data.

The console now depends on shared/ (api-contracts generated by the PWA, i18n common/format, design-system web copy). Whenever shared/ or the backend contract changes, run in this order: `pnpm contract:generate` in pwa/, then `pnpm contract:generate` and `pnpm check` in frontend/admin-console. A small root script (or CI job) that runs both apps' checks would make this automatic (DI-11).

Plan the pilot's staff accounts before AC6 (OQ-10): two ADM accounts are needed for any ADM-only four-eyes change (kill switch off, a rate change over 20 %, plans, retention, role grants), plus at least one MOD and one CRV. The first ADM comes from the AC11.T3 runbook; the second must be granted by four-eyes, so create both before the four-eyes rule matters (backend bootstrap or the dev tool in dev).

AC3 can be smaller than planned: security headers (D-05), the operation map with roles, reason/purpose/4EYES/ETAG/IDEM/ASYNC/AAL3 flags, and the route allowlist source (src/lib/api/generated/operations.ts) are ready. The forwarder should build its allowlist straight from ADMIN_OPERATIONS (method + path template + host), never from a hand-written list.
